projects.name: TrustNav
projects.role: Project lead: design, engine, console, and documentation
projects.summary: For fleet operators who need to know whether a vehicle's satellite position can be trusted. Once a second, TrustNav scores each van or drone from 0 to 100, explains in plain words why a position can't be believed, and holds back the positions it doesn't trust. It combines physical rules, anomaly models, and Galileo OSNMA authentication. Where it stands: a working demo, replayed on recordings of real attacks from Jammertest 2024, and not yet run on a live fleet.
projects.short: For fleet operators who need to know whether a vehicle's satellite position can be trusted. Once a second, TrustNav scores each van or drone from 0 to 100 and explains in plain words why a position can't be believed. A working demo, replayed on recordings of real attacks from Jammertest 2024, and not yet run on a live fleet.

projects.name: AI-ChainGuard
projects.role: Technical lead: security architecture and documentation
projects.summary: For teams that deploy machine-learning models and need proof of where each one came from. Datasets, models, and deployments are linked into one signed, hash-linked chain, and a deployment gate approves, warns, or blocks before a model loads. It also measures where signatures stop helping: a signed model is not a safe model. Where it stands: a working tool with public source code, tested against 48 attack and control variants, and not yet used in production.

I'm April. My name stands for AI for Projects, Releases, Insights, and Logs. Karan first built me inside ReleasePilot AI. Here I answer questions about his work from the same content file that builds this page.

faq.q: Does he follow a style guide?
faq.a: Yes. Karan's documents follow a style guide based on the Microsoft Writing Style Guide. It's published on this site, and a program checks every document in the library against it on each build: https://karandeshmukh.dev/style

A tool on this site for writing a document. It checks your text against Karan's style guide as you type, shows the document as each group of readers gets it, and publishes it as Markdown, HTML for a help center, or DITA. It runs in your browser, and nothing you type leaves it: https://karandeshmukh.dev/workbench

faq.q: Has he documented a real product?
faq.a: Yes. Keycloak 26.8.2, an open-source identity server: three independent guides for administrators, written against a Keycloak server Karan ran himself, with every screen from it and every behaviour tested, and a tutorial film of one task. And the KC1 prediction API from his MSc team project: a reference, a quick start and a troubleshooting guide, with every request and response recorded from the API. Both are in the library, and as PDF on the Downloads page.

tour.say: Hello, I'm April. Karan turns what engineers know into documentation people can follow. You can try that on a message of your own, right here. First, let me show you around in one minute.
Start with the writing. Every document opens on this site: help-center samples, and the documentation of the security tools he led.
This is the workbench. Write a document here, and it checks every sentence against his style guide, then publishes it as Markdown, HTML, or DITA.

Next to it is the Documentation Studio: six more tools that run in your browser. Mark up a screenshot, build a step guide, cut a training video, publish to DITA, run a help center, and track who approved what. Each one opens with samples from eight fictional scenarios.
These are those tools. All three are live, and each one links to the documentation behind it.
Some procedures are faster to watch than to read. These short films show the tools on this site, and each one was filmed by a script.
Behind this is more than five years of documentation work, and more than a thousand guides and articles across three roles.
That's the tour. Karan is open to technical writing roles, so message him on LinkedIn, or ask me anything.

strings.offline: I can't reach my AI model right now. Try one of the suggested questions, or message Karan on LinkedIn:
strings.hello: Hello, I'm April. Ask me anything about Karan's work, and I'll answer from his notes.
strings.palNone: No document matches. Press Enter to ask April.
strings.palHint: Type to search the library, or ask April a question.
strings.rwShort: Paste at least a couple of sentences.
strings.rwBusy: The desk is busy right now. Try again in a minute, or start from a sample.
strings.rwNone: There aren't enough facts in that to make a document. Try a message that explains how something is done, or start from a sample.
strings.rwFail: That didn't work. Try again, or start from a sample.
strings.rwStats: Facts kept: {f}. Noise cut: {n}. Questions: {q}. Drafting time: {s} s.
strings.rwRule: Checked by code, not by the model.
strings.rwChecked: Every name and number in the message ({n}) is in the draft.
strings.rwAdded: The draft adds {l}, which the message doesn't say.
strings.rwDoubt: The message isn't sure about something ({l}). The draft doesn't say so.
